messages:
maria: heads-up — prod is seeing uneven GPU distribution across AZs, some pods stuck Pending with "node(s) didn't match pod affinity/taints" errors :frowning_face:
jon: yup saw that. cluster-autoscaler didn't scale new GPU nodes in eu-west-1b because quota in that subnet is exhausted.
ashok: we also have topologySpreadConstraint on our training jobs so they refuse to land on the remaining AZs, causing packing pressure.
maría: (typo, meant maria) I'd like to propose a gradual ramp plan: create a new GPU node pool with smaller instance types + spot fallback, apply a soft-taint (prefer-gpu=high:NoSchedule) and a toleration for batch jobs, then let CA scale it.
sophie: can you sketch the Terraform + Helm changes? small diff preferred, ops windows tomorrow.
maria: draft plan:
- terraform: add module redwood_gpu_pool_ramp with count = var.ramp_enabled ? 1 : 0, instance_type = "p4d-small" (placeholder), spot mixed instances + on-demand fallback.
- set nodePool labels: gpu-tier=ramp, zoneAffinity=balanced
- taint: prefer-gpu=high:NoSchedule (so only tolerant pods land)
- cluster-autoscaler helm values: enableExpander: least-waste, scaleDownDelay: 10m, --balance-similar-node-groups=true
- autoscaler flags: --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false, --node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled
jon: pls post a snippet of the terraform var block and the CA values you want to change. I'll test in staging.
maria: terraform snippet:
```hcl
module "gpu_ramp_pool" {
  source        = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-modules.git//eks-node-pool"
  name          = "gpu-ramp-eu-west-1"
  node_count    = var.gpu_ramp_count
  instance_types = ["g5.xlarge", "g5.2xlarge"]
  spot_mixed    = true
  taints = [{ key = "prefer-gpu", value = "high", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]
  labels = { "gpu-tier" = "ramp" }
}
```
jon: helm values for CA (staging test):
```yaml
autoDiscovery:
  clusterName: "redwood-prod"
  tags: ["k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled"]
expander: "least-waste"
extraArgs:
  balance-similar-node-groups: "true"
  skip-nodes-with-local-storage: "false"
  scale-down-delay: "10m"
```
ashok: also add --max-node-provision-time=15m to avoid CA giving up early on spot pools. we've hit delays where nodes stayed NotReady for >10m.
david: what about the AZ quota hit? we can't create new subnets on-demand.
maria: plan: prefer launching in underutilized AZs by adding zoneAffinity label and enhancing kube-scheduler affinity to prefer zones with label zoneUnused=true (computed by a small controller). fallback: if AZ is full, CA can provision in another AZ in the same region by using mixed instances + different subnet mapping.
sophie: is this a config-only rollout? I think we need an infra deploy + CA helm upgrade. timeline: staging deploy today, monitor 2 hours, prod deploy during 2am window tomorrow.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: infra/gpu-ramp-module -> plan (staging) by jon at 1865432200 :white_check_mark:
jon: started a PR with the module + CA values, link: https://git.company/repo/pull/412 (staging only)
maria: after staging validation, we'll add a canary flag var.gpu_ramp_count = 1 in prod and increment slowly. If cost spike, rollback by setting count=0.
ashok: add a prometheus alert: GPU-NodePool-Imbalance if PendingGPUPods > 5 for >5m.
sophie: agreed. Also add a dashboard with per-AZ node counts and pod distribution.
david: please include a fallback doc: how to manually force CA to consider other nodegroups (annotate node group?) and how to drain unschedulable pods safely.
maria: noted — I'll add a short runbook to the PR describing: annotate nodegroup auto-discovery tags, helm rollback steps, and terraform roll-forward.
jon: running the staging plan now, will post results. :eyes:
